clauses.reason: The order directs that on Monday, June 21, 1976 the flag of the United States be flown at half-staff on federal buildings, grounds and naval vessels in the District of Columbia and throughout the United States and its territories and possessions, and at embassies, consular offices and other facilities abroad, as a mark of respect to Francis E. Meloy, Jr. and Robert O. Waring. The command is limited to that one day, so it was spent at the end of 1976-06-21 (inclusive; exclusive reading 1976-06-20).

research_rationale:
EO 11923 (signed 1976-06-17) is a single half-staff command under section 4 of Proclamation 3044 of March 1, 1954, as amended, for Monday, June 21, 1976. The held Federal Register text was read in full; it has one operative clause (domestic and foreign facilities are two sentences of the same command). It ended by its own terms on 1976-06-21. A search of the held corpus for the number found only the order's own text.

savings.reason: The order orders a flag display on one named day and creates no right, duty or rule beyond it; none survives June 21, 1976.
